_why: Switches that are NOT the switch of an integration instance: the row is another kind of thing, or an instance-like row that is not an integration-instances record yet. Each carries its reason. The list only shrinks: a row that becomes an instance (planning#440 steps 4+) leaves it in the same change.

capMethods.addons.cap.ts:setCapabilityProviderEnabl: a capability provider binding of an addon, not an integration instance
capMethods.core-blocks.cap.ts:setEnabled: a core block has its own record kind and cap, not an integration-instances provider
capMethods.notification-rules.cap.ts:setRuleEnabled: a notification rule is a rule row with its own cap, not an integration instance
capMethods.schedulers.cap.ts:setEnabled: a scheduler job has its own cap and store, not an integration-instances provider
capMethods.packages/addon-post-analysis/src/notific: a rule's per-target switch inside a notification rule row, not an integration instance
capMethods.packages/addon-notifiers/src/nc-target-a: the shipped viewer still calls it; a thin delegate onto the instance door. Removed with the viewer release that uses the door
capMethods.stream-broker.cap.ts:setRtspEnabled: the broker's RTSP server toggle, a node setting, not an instance

setInstanceEnabledImplementations.packages/addon-notifiers/src/nc-target-a: calls the door's setInstanceEnabled for the shipped viewer's nc.setMyTargetEnabled; it stores nothing (removed with that action)
setInstanceEnabledImplementations.packages/types/src/addon/notification-ta: a per-user notification target: the wrapper only refuses a caller who does not own the row, then delegates to RecordIntegrationInstances.setInstanceEnabled (no second stored field)
setInstanceEnabledImplementations.packages/system/src/builtins/storage-orc: a storage location keeps ONE typed state, mode, read only through storage-location-mode.ts (D385/D386); the row switch writes that state, never a second enabled field
setInstanceEnabledImplementations.server/backend/src/core/addon/instance-l: the hub half of the one switch: for a FIXED builtin (no instance body) it writes the registry flag, the only store of that row; for every other row it forwards to the addon's provider. integrations.update refuses enabled for everyone (D1015)
